thread:
Maria Chen: hitting an odd one with the Python SDK + Dedicated deployment behind our customer proxy/vpc. Intermittent 'certificate verify failed' on some requests, works if I retry. Seen with base_url pointed at the private control plane and a custom CA bundle. :confused:

Ben Patel: can you paste the minimal snippet you’re running? is this sync or async?

Maria Chen: async. trying to load test a few hundred concurrent chat calls. minimal snippet below (sanitized):

Maria Chen: ```py
from redwood import AsyncClient

client = AsyncClient(api_key=..., base_url="https://private-redwood.example", proxies={"https": "http://proxy.internal:3128"}, verify="/etc/ssl/custom_ca.pem")

async def call():
    r = await client.chat.create(messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "hi"}])
    return r
```

Maria Chen: logs look like: TLSHandshakeError: [SSL: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED] certificate verify failed: unable to get local issuer certificate (_ssl.c:XXXX)

Sanjay Rao: does the SDK use httpx under the hood for async? if so, verify param should be respected, but proxies+pooling + sslcontext can get tricky. which package versions?

Maria Chen: httpx 0.23.3, ssl from Python 3.11.3. requests isn't involved. Also noticed failures only under high concurrency and only to a couple of hosts in the same infra region. Lower qps -> no failures.

Ben Patel: two quick hypothesis: 1) connection pooling is reusing connections with an SSLContext that was created without the custom CA (race on client creation vs first request), 2) proxy doing TLS interception and sometimes returning a different cert chain. can you repro with a single AsyncClient instance vs creating many clients?

Maria Chen: good point. creating a single client and sharing it reduced the failures a lot. creating per-coro clients -> spikes. I’ll repro with shared client only and report back.

Maria Chen: also tried forcing ssl.SSLContext and passing it in: verify=ssl_context where ssl_context.load_verify_locations(custom_ca). that made errors disappear in my quick runs.

Sanjay Rao: that suggests the SDK path that constructs SSLContext for httpx AsyncClient might not be using the provided verify path consistently when proxies are present. Could be a bug where we call httpx._some_internal to build context and ignore 'verify' in some code path.

Ben Patel: would you be able to catch a dump of the cert chain returned when failing? ops-bot can help route a tcpdump or mitm log if needed. also wondering if httpx http2 or h11 behavior changes anything.

Maria Chen: attaching a small log snippet: ```
ERROR TLSHandshakeError host=private-redwood.example
peer cert issuer=C=US, O=CustCorp CA
verify path=/etc/ssl/custom_ca.pem
ssl_context certs_loaded=True
```

devex-bot: created ticket DEVEX-1427 for investigation (assign: @ben.patel).

Ben Patel: thanks. I’ll reproduce locally with a proxy simulator. possible short-term workaround: set REDWOOD_CA_BUNDLE env var pointing to PEM and ensure SDK reads that before building clients. we should also document this pattern in quickstart for Dedicated/Private.

Sanjay Rao: feature request: SDK should accept a top-level `ca_bundle` or `tls` config param (typed in stubs) that 1) always constructs a single SSLContext during client init, 2) honors it across sync/async and proxy code paths, and 3) uses it for connection pool reinitialization after proxy change. can we add typing for that to make it discoverable?

Maria Chen: +1 on typing. I tripped over this because IDE signature didn't show verify param for AsyncClient in our SDK wrapper.

Ben Patel: logged improvement: DEVEX-1428 — "py-sdk: ca_bundle arg + typed TLS config + env var precedence". I'll add a docs blurb to dedicated onboarding (how to set CA + proxies).

Maria Chen: also note for the team: when using proxies that do TLS interception, you might get different issuer chains per edge node; that makes strict per-connection verification more fragile if only some leaf intermediates are present in your bundle. adding the full chain to the PEM helps.

Sanjay Rao: action items:
- Ben: reproduce + patch candidate to ensure verify path used consistently (DEVEX-1427)
- Ben: implement ca_bundle arg + types + env var handling (DEVEX-1428)
- Docs: add Dedicated quickstart section for custom CA + proxy (Ben/Sally)
- Maria: paste repro case when you have the per-coro creation pattern (so we can add an integration test)

Maria Chen: thanks — appreciate quick triage. workaround for anyone hitting this: share one AsyncClient instance, or construct and pass an ssl.SSLContext loaded with your CA as `verify`.

ops-bot: note — customer uses an HA proxy cluster; saw TLS interception logs around 2024-10-05T14:22Z matching Maria's failures. forwarding to infra.
